brief: Weekly positioning note argues sentiment and flows are too defensive across five dimensions, implying upside risk if unwound. US equities saw the largest net buying in five weeks and European equities the largest in five months, suggesting investors were too short. CTAs sold $47bn of global equities over the past month ($38bn last week per one desk estimate, $39bn per the systematic model, bringing length to $91bn, 62nd percentile); models predict a small further downside overshoot before CTAs flip to buyers over a one-month horizon, and CTAs have already turned buyers of US equities. Global equity fund inflows jumped to +$80bn last week from +$10bn the prior week. GS's Sentiment Indicator fell to -0.9 (lowest since August 2025) and AAII bearishness hit 53.3% (highest in 16 months), with Privorotsky quoted urging optimism when everyone shares the same worry list. CFTC data and desk anecdotes show Long Onlys still trimming, not yet reengaged, ahead of this week's Trump/Xi summit. Separately, hedge fund gross leverage rose to 309.2%, and asset managers were net sellers of S&P futures.
